title: Unit 1 — Narrative tenses
subtitle: Outcomes 2ed B1 Intermediate · Grammar, conversations and writing

blocks.title: Narrative tenses
blocks.rule: Use the past simple for completed events, the past continuous for an action in progress or background, and the past perfect for an event that happened before another past event.

exampleGroups.label: Past simple + past perfect
exampleGroups.help: The past perfect makes the earlier action clear.

examples.text: When I arrived, the class had already started.
She went bright red after she had used the wrong word.

exampleGroups.label: Past continuous
exampleGroups.help: Use it for an action that was in progress at a particular moment.

examples.text: We were driving through town when I saw a friend.
The car was moving towards a tree.

blocks.title: Link the two past actions
paragraphs: Complete each sentence. Use one verb in the past simple and one verb in the past perfect.
Write the complete sentence. Contractions such as had → ’d are accepted.

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.rule: Link the later action with the earlier action. Use the past simple for the later event and the past perfect for the event that happened first.

exampleGroups.label: Example
exampleGroups.help: The film started first. We arrived afterwards.

examples.text: The film started. We arrived. → When we arrived, the film had already started.

blocks.title: John was telling me …
paragraphs: Put the lines in the correct order to make three conversations.
Use the arrow buttons to move each line. In conversation 2, the two short replies “Yes” and “Yes, that’s right” may exchange places; both textbook versions are accepted.

blocks.question: Conversation 1 — Amy and the guitar

items.label: Amy was telling me you’ve taken up the guitar.
No, I have private lessons. My tutor is really good – very patient.
Classical. I like listening to rock but don’t think I’m a Jimi Hendrix type!
Yeah, that’s right.
Is he? So, what style do you play?
Great! Are you teaching yourself to play?

blocks.question: Conversation 2 — A part-time job

items.label: Paul was telling me you’re looking for a part-time job.
Well, if I hear of anything, I’ll let you know.
Well, maybe restaurant or bar work.
Have you had any luck yet?
Yes, that’s right.
Like a waiter or something?
No, but I’ve only just started looking.
What sort of job are you looking for?
Yes.

blocks.explanation: The two short affirmative replies can be used in positions 2 and 6 in either order.

blocks.question: Conversation 3 — Going to Argentina

items.label: Katrina was telling me you’re going to Argentina.
How long will you be away for?
Well, good luck, I hope it goes well.
That’s amazing. What are you going to do?
About twelve months, I think.
Yes, news travels fast!
I’ve got a job in a language school.
